summary.text: A 35-year-old woman, gravida II, para I, presented at 32 weeks and four days of gestation with labor pain and ruptured membranes after unremarkable pregnancy monitoring and received corticosteroids. A 2000 g female neonate was delivered by cesarean section after 35 hours with Apgar scores of 7 and 8. At birth the neonate had armor-like thickened yellowish scales, deep erythematous fissures, ectropion, eclabium, a flattened nasal bridge, rudimentary ears and absent eyebrows, eyelashes and hair.

Harlequin ichthyosis was diagnosed clinically. ABCA12 genetic testing on day 9 of life, with parental consent, identified a homozygous pathogenic variant c.179G>C, p.(Arg60Pro), confirming the diagnosis. Laboratory tests revealed early hypoglycemia, metabolic imbalances and neonatal anemia requiring transfusion.

The neonate was admitted to the NICU in a humidified incubator with cardiorespiratory monitoring, supplemental oxygen, an umbilical venous catheter, parenteral nutrition, intravenous antibiotics and paracetamol. In the second week of life fever and clinical deterioration with elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin suggested systemic infection, and antibiotics were escalated and antifungal treatment added. Systemic retinoids were not started pending genetic confirmation. Skin care softened the plates by around day 10, but the skin stayed rigid with necrosis and bleeding fissures.

Around day 30 of life the neonate had recurrent oxygen desaturation and bradycardia with poor respiratory effort despite maximized incubator oxygen. Endotracheal intubation was attempted but was not technically possible because of facial and cervical skin rigidity and limited mouth opening. The infant died shortly thereafter despite resuscitation efforts, on the 30th day of life.
